dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: Ours additionally accepts the case `fileCanonicalPath.equals(dirCanonicalPath)` (e.g. entry name "" or "."), which the official fix rejects. This is not exploitable — a directory entry resolving to dir itself makes mkdirsQuietly(dir) a no-op, and a file entry resolving to dir makes `new FileOutputStream(dir)` throw FileNotFoundException — but it is a small behavioral divergence from the reference and relies on downstream failure rather than the guard.

dir.getCanonicalPath() is recomputed (a syscall) for every zip entry, whereas the official fix hoists `canonicalDestinationDirPath` above the loop. Purely a performance nit on large archives; no security impact.

The exception message uses `file.getName()` (leaf name only, e.g. "evil.txt") instead of `entry.getName()` (the full malicious entry path). Cosmetic/diagnostic only — makes forensic triage of a blocked entry slightly less informative than the official message.

result.root_cause: processZipStream built a destination File directly from the attacker-controlled ZipEntry name (`new File(dir, entry.getName())`) and passed it to filesystem sinks (mkdirsQuietly and FileOutputStream) without ever verifying that the resolved real path stays inside the temp extraction directory, allowing `../` (Zip Slip) entries to write arbitrary files outside it.
result.summary: Our patch is a correct, class-closing fix: it canonicalizes both the extraction directory and the resolved entry destination and enforces containment at the exact trust boundary in InputStreamHelper.processZipStream, immediately after `new File(dir, entry.getName())` and before every sink (directory mkdirs, parent mkdirs, and FileOutputStream), so all three tainted traces are dominated by the guard. This is the CWE-022 defense-of-record (canonicalize-then-verify, not `../` blocklisting) and is semantically the same mechanism and location as the official Snyk-referenced fix, with 1.0 file overlap. The POV no longer reproduces, both regression suites pass, and benign extraction is preserved (the `File.separator` suffix avoids sibling-prefix false positives). Only cosmetic divergences remain: an extra allowance for file==dir, per-entry recomputation of the dir canonical path, and a less informative exception message.
